Claire (sec): Heads up — we just got a DSAR erase request for a customer on Private (VPC) who uses their own KMS. Their legal says no holds but our retention system shows a recent retention exception flag from a month ago. Can we confirm the canonical deletion path?
Sanjay (eng): Do we have a keystore handshake flow for customer-managed keys? I thought Private flows required a signed authorization from the tenant to unwrap/delete.
Michael (infra): Correct — for private deployments we never hold plaintext keys. We have a signed-delete flow: erasure worker requests a Key Authorization Token (KAT) from the privpath control plane which is signed by customer KMS. Need RBAC to let the erasure worker read the keystore metadata only.
Anuj (privacy): Important: before we start the erase, legal needs proof there is no active hold. Legal Ops, can you confirm?
Legal Ops: I see no active litigation hold on our tracker. The earlier retention exception was a short-term export; looks like it expired. Still, we'll need a deletion receipt and audit proof.
Claire (sec): OK — two action items: 1) short-lived RBAC to let erasure worker fetch metadata + KAT request; 2) ensure audit log contains the KAT id, keystore fingerprint, and erasure receipt.
Sanjay (eng): For the RBAC, propose creating a scoped SA: `erasure-worker@redwood-priv.iam` with a single permission `privpath.keystore.getMetadata` and `privpath.key.requestKAT`. TTL 15m and must be minted by `admin-oncall` via the breakglass flow.
Michael (infra): I can add an ephemeral role-binding script. Example quick command we can use in emergencies:
```bash
# mint ephemeral SA binding
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding erasure-worker@redwood-priv.iam \
  --member="serviceAccount:token-broker@redwood.iam" \
  --role="roles/privpath.keystoreAccessor" \
  --condition="expression=request.time < timestamp(\"2026-04-01T12:00:00Z\"),title=ephemeral_erasure"
```
Claire (sec): Nice, include a short checklist that `admin-oncall` must follow and a required sign-off from Legal Ops before minting. Also: record the ticket ID in the audit event.
Anuj (privacy): On audit format — please include these fields in the erasure audit event: `subject_id`, `requester_proof`, `keystore_fingerprint`, `KAT_id`, `erasure_worker_id`, `pre_erase_counts`, `post_erase_counts`, `operator_ticket_id`.
Sanjay (eng): Adding to that: we should log the signature verification step and the KMS key ID (but not any key material). Also emit a compact hash of the object IDs removed so Legal can verify without holding PII.
erasure-bot: Erasure job 87321 queued -> pending RBAC. (reaction :hourglass_flowing_sand:)
Michael (infra): One edge: if the customer's KMS fails to respond (timeouts) we need a fallback. Proposal: mark as "deferred" and notify Legal + Support to reach out to customer KMS operator. Do NOT attempt any cryptographic workaround.
Legal Ops: Agreed — deferred + escalation only. We need email proof from customer KMS operator to mark as complete if they manually remove keys.
Claire (sec): Vulnerability triage note: if granting ephemeral RBAC could surface a privilege escalation path, we must review `token-broker` and `admin-oncall` minting code. Sanjay, please open a vuln ticket and assign to infra.
Sanjay (eng): Will do. Ticket created: INFRA-9854. I'll include code pointers and the minting script.
Anuj (privacy): Final ask — produce a deletion receipt template Legal can send to the customer that includes the audit hash and KAT_id but never the raw key id or PII. I'll draft.
Claire (sec): Great. Michael — can you add the script to the oncall runbook and enforce a 15m TTL? Also add an explicit audit emitter step that sends the JSON receipt to the retention-audit S3 with server-side encryption.
Michael (infra): Yep. I'll push a runbook PR and ping here when it's live.
erasure-bot: Erasure job 87321 status updated -> waiting for RBAC minting (ADMIN_ONCALL).
Claire (sec): Thanks everyone — summary: Legal confirmed no hold, infra to provision ephemeral RBAC with 15m TTL, erasure worker will request KAT, audit fields agreed, vulnerability ticket opened, deferred path for KMS failures. Followups: @Sanjay to open vuln ticket, @Michael to PR runbook, @Anuj to draft receipt.
Sanjay (eng): I'll be in touch after triage. :thumbsup:
Michael (infra): PR #4221 opened for runbook, includes minting script and examples.
Anuj (privacy): Draft receipt posted to the privacy drive, link in the ticket.
Claire (sec): Closing loop here — if anything blocks the erasure worker start, label the slack thread with `blocked-erasure` and escalate. Thanks.
